notes:
Batch 1 covers n 350–699, all 350 names. Points to check, highest impact first:
1. Crane, Cranes, Crané (463–465) are left unknown. In committee and Heligoland entries 'Crane' means Common Crane (Grus grus), but Scottish and Irish keepers used it for Grey Heron (e.g. three to five on June 7th). Resolve each observation by source.
2. 'Common' (365) is a split fragment. The example is Common [Thrush], but the other 5 observations may come from other compounds. Left unknown.
3. Cormorant and Cormorants (442–443, 211 observations) are set to Great Cormorant, but keepers likely included Shags. Consider genus-level for shag-heavy stations.
4. Common Skua (415–417) is set to Great Skua, following period British usage (Unst breeding). Dirty Allan(s) (525–528) is Arctic Skua, IOC name Parasitic Jaeger.
5. Dovekies (539) is set to Black Guillemot because 'Rotges' (Little Auk) are listed separately. Check the source.
6. Copperfinch(es) (439–440) are left at genus Fringilla. The editor guessed Brambling, but 'Copperfinch' is a West Country dialect name for Chaffinch.
7. Heading names extracted as species: CUCULIDÆ and CYPSELIDÆ and their garbles (488–489, 492, 502–503, 507) are set to Cuckoo and Common Swift, since only those occur in Britain. FALCONIDÆ (612, 614) is a group, because the period family covered all diurnal raptors. FRINGILLIDÆ (667–669) is a family. Check that the extraction didn't take a heading in place of the named species line (669 especially).
8. OCR fixes I applied: 'Fr./Fring. alpina' (646, 657) read as Tringa alpina = Dunlin; 'Fledge Sparrow' = Hedge Sparrow; 'Crowds' = Crows; 'Faicons' = Falcons; 'Gall' = Gull; 'Corn Genk' = Corn Crake (least sure; check the scan); 'sole piper' = Sandpiper.
9. Garbles left unknown: Easdriballs (562), ecroolansGeese (564), Fpmetorqitilia (645, probably Jynx torquilla = Wryneck, possibly Saxicola torquata), French Sparrows (656), Furse Cap (675), 'different species' (521, a phrase, not a name).
10. Taxonomy depends on the IOC version you use. I used Curruca for whitethroats, Coloeus for jackdaw, Gulosus for shag, Mareca and Spatula for ducks, Hydrobates for storm petrels, Linaria for linnet and twite, 'Western House Martin', 'Western Osprey', 'Common Firecrest', 'Common Murre', and the loon names. Redpolls (599, 651, 655, 663, 666) are Acanthis flammea / A. cabaret: check against your version, as recent lists lump redpolls.
11. Smaller doubts: Common Godwit (387) is left at genus Limosa (the name was used for both godwits). Common Crow (379–380) is at genus Corvus (Carrion Crow or Rook). Emberiza passerina (585) is set to Reed Bunting, eastern form; rule out Pallas's Reed Bunting. G. gallinula (677) is Jack Snipe, not Moorhen. 'Gallinula' (688) is set to Rallidae, but could be Jack Snipe. Common Buntings flock of 250 at Sumburgh in November (373) may be Snow Buntings. Common Whitethroat killed Feb. 21st (432) and female Redstart Nov. 3rd (616) are odd dates. Crested Larks (472–473) would be a rare record; check. Dotterels (536) is set to genus Charadrius, as keepers may mean Ringed Plover. Common Gulls (391) may mean ordinary gulls in some entries. Common Sparrows with '(?)' (366) are kept apart from House Sparrow (perhaps Tree Sparrow), so set to genus Passer.
12. Joined names that could be split into two rows: 'Common and Arctic Terns' (368, at genus Sterna), 'Curlew and Stint' (496, group Waders, 13 observations), 'Cole Tit or a Great Tit' (357, family Paridae).
